newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bankers find more money in dormant accounts.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bankers find more money in dormant accounts.

text.p: The Swiss Bankers' Association said on Wednesday that their latest search for pre-1945 accounts that may belong to Holocaust victims had turned up about 17 million Swiss francs more than they had reported last year.
"The total current value of these accounts is 60.2 million Swiss francs ($42 million)," the association said in a statement.

The banks said last year they had found around 43 million francs in about 1,000 accounts, opened by non-Swiss before the end of World War Two and whose owners had not been heard from in at least 10 years.
The search criteria mean that some account holders may have lost touch for reasons other than the Holocaust.
In total, there are 1,872 names associated with 1,756 separate accounts (including joint accounts), the statement said.
It was released ahead of a news conference where the bankers' association was due to present a list of pre-1945 account holders who may have perished in the Holocaust.
Swiss banks are publishing the unprecedented three-page list in newspapers in 28 countries and on the Internet, breaking with a tradition of secrecy after criticism by Jewish groups.
